_comment: This is an example config. install.sh creates a working controller/config.json with passwords filled in. Set your platform(s) and the backup_file via the dashboard Settings tab (or edit primary_server/primary_key/restreams and backup_file here by hand).
_comment_public_host: The public IP/hostname of this server -- used to build the OBS Server URL and the dashboard/obs-source links (restreamctl.sh credentials, install.sh's own printed instructions). install.sh asks for this on every run, since it's not a secret and might change.
_comment_outputs: Platforms are managed from the dashboard Settings tab (add/edit/remove) and Control tab (on/off) -- easier than editing here. Each platform stores server + key separately (exactly the two fields a platform gives you, e.g. OBS's Server + Stream Key); the controller joins them into the push URL and auto-adds :443/app for Kick/AWS IVS (*.live-video.net). Both rtmp:// and rtmps:// work. primary is the mandatory main platform (can't be removed); restreams are extra, toggleable ones. The 'enabled' flags are managed by the Control tab. Aggregate failsafe: the broadcast is stopped hard only if NONE of the enabled platforms can be reached at start; if at least one connects, failed ones just retry/toast.
_comment_output: The controller determines the backup video's resolution/fps/channels itself via ffprobe of the live stream on every broadcast start -- no need to set them here. These two fields only affect the QUALITY of the one-time backup transcode (when it doesn't match live): the video/audio bitrate of the resulting backup.prepared.mp4.
_comment_timeouts: Two-phase silent-drop detection (CLAUDE.md, v12/v14). connect_timeout_ms: how long to wait for OBS's first frame after it connects (MediaMTX's own readTimeout, minimum 2500 -- real OBS needs several seconds for encoder warm-up + first keyframe, longer than a synthetic test source). read_timeout_ms: once data is flowing, how fast to react to a stalled network without dropping the OBS connection (minimum 300). mediamtx.yml's readTimeout is recalculated as their sum on every MediaMTX start -- don't edit it there directly.
_comment_icmp_ping: Control tab Ping column: false (default) = TCP-connect time to the platform's RTMP/RTMPS port (works without privileges); true = system ICMP ping (avg RTT), closer to a classic ping but may be blocked by a firewall or need privileges (the ping binary must allow a normal user -- see README) -- if it fails the column shows a dash. Toggle it on the Settings tab.
